prompt:
Create a new polished HAVENLINE 3D game concept sheet titled "EXPANDED COMPATIBLE NETWORKS" with a small subtitle "PROPOSED CONNECTION STUDY". Landscape, four large meaningful panels in a clean 2 by 2 grid, peach studio ground, soft warm lighting, crisp toy-like 3D modeling, blue/orange Havenline palette. This is a new connected use study of the exact supplied machines and interfaces, not a redesign. Every conveyor is low solid ORANGE housing with YELLOW rim, dense black transverse rollers, blue lower trim and silver bridge plates. Any height change has a continuous supported orange ramp or adapter. No tall spindly legs. The supplied small ordinary pickups and Character1 proportions are fixed. Keep resource units visibly handheld; make piles from several units. Character1 has glasses, short black hair, beard, navy winter jacket with cream lining and orange trim, dark trousers and brown boots.

REFERENCES, IN THIS ORDER: (1) exact approved blue storage house exterior and four port positions; (2) exact local utility receive/dispatch mechanism and wall sleeves; (3) exact register-free material self-service counter, flat bundled planks and single rectangular stone block tokens; (4) current saw, typed feeder, retained tracked quarry drill and its explicitly proposed parked stone-to-block cassette; (5) current smelter and hand metal bench; (6) owner-approved ordinary pickup size and fixed Character1 anchor. Preserve all these identities. The new sheet connects existing compatible ports using real modeled joined roller sections. Floating route arrows or labels cannot replace a physical connection. Keep space between neighboring belts; do not run a conveyor through a machine, house wall, control wheel, access aisle or another conveyor. Make each source OUT to destination IN visibly traceable in its entire local scene.

TOP LEFT — "TIMBER MODE / PLANKS". A raised three-quarter overview of one complete serial route, with enough empty ground to read it: a small timber-only raw log feeder leads to the exact timber saw bench, saw OUT carries flat rectangular bundled PLANKS along an unbroken roller path into the storage house's low left-wall UTILITY IN below its window. A SEPARATE parallel UTILITY OUT sleeve leaves that same storage house, carries the same small plank bundles along a different unbroken roller path and terminates in the actual curved inlet and silver landing of the material counter labeled PLANKS. Place the saw/source behind or beside the incoming lane; place the counter on the outgoing lane in front-left so all joins can be seen. Show the complete snow-topped blue/orange storage house with double front doors and a clear apron. At the two wall ports label "PLANKS IN" and "PLANKS OUT". At least one visible white arrow points into IN and one out of OUT, matching actual flow. There is no outside belt connecting OUT directly back to IN. The house's internal indexed storage transfer is the only relation between them. Raw rounded logs exist only before the saw; only flat bound plank bundles after it. A small green cash pile is on a separate plate at the far counter end. No register, no clerk. A Character1 visitor can approach the counter and the front doors along clear ground.

TOP RIGHT — "MINERAL MODE / BLOCKS". This is a SEPARATE selected mode/example of the same storage interfaces, not simultaneous incompatible cargo in one sleeve. Another complete serial route uses the retained tracked blue quarry drill and timber derrick parked behind its separate low blue/orange conversion cassette, exactly like reference 4. Label the cassette "PROPOSED PARKED DOCK". Rough raw tan stone enters its RAW STONE IN. Rectangular pale stone BLOCKS leave its clearly labeled BLOCK OUT onto a physically joined continuous roller path to the storage house's low UTILITY IN. The separate UTILITY OUT path carries those same rectangular block tokens to the actual curved inlet of the material counter labeled BLOCKS. Label the house ports "BLOCKS IN" and "BLOCKS OUT". No route into the food ports, fuel hatch, window or double doors. Do not connect the quarry drill itself to an invented socket; the parked processing cassette is separate and explicit. Keep the same snow-roofed blue/orange house, window, usable doors, indexed utility handling and a separate little cash plate at the counter. No raw-stone sales, no mixed timber/mineral feed. Each visible curve, height transition and terminal silver plate physically meets the next component without a gap.

BOTTOM LEFT — "IRON TRANSFER / SHEET MODE". A connected industrial scene, not three disconnected product photos. Preserve the exact round vertical blue coal smelter with orange glowing fire door, stone base, flue and dial. Separate ore and coal feeder approaches remain on its intake side. Its opposite IRON OUT roller tray connects through a continuous low orange/yellow roller path and silver coupler directly into the hand metal bench's rear IRON IN rack. Keep several dark-gray rectangular iron bars along this one connected route. Preserve the exact wooden blue-frame bench, two horizontal silver rollers, upper orange handwheel and separate parts bin. Its selected sheet mode creates a small neat silver sheet stack at its dedicated output collection tray. Label that end "MANUAL PICKUP" and leave the parts bin empty in this mode. No material counter, money, storage sale chute or automatic sheets-to-parts chain here. Clear unobstructed front control/service ground reaches the smelter fire door, dial, bench handwheel and output pickup. A normal-size Character1 stands on that clear ground, not on a belt.

BOTTOM RIGHT — "IRON JOIN / CLEAR ACCESS". A genuinely opposing elevated view of the SAME connected smelter-to-bench assembly, arranged so the silver joined bridge and the bench IRON IN receiving rack are unobscured. Show the iron bars at the joined throat and along the incoming roller surface, with one concise flow arrow from smelter OUT into bench IN. The bench sheet output remains an accessible MANUAL PICKUP tray; no active simultaneous parts output. The foreground shows continuous clear walkable ground for the front controls, not a conveyor across their reach. Keep geometry and machine identities consistent across the two industrial views. Use a useful close view, not a decorative angle that hides the actual coupling.

GLOBAL: These are proposed static connections, not a claim of implemented automation. Only PLANKS and BLOCKS appear at the material sales counters; cash remains separate and never rides a conveyor. No new product, wallet, menu, animal, recipe quantity, industrial sales, random staff, painted outside roads, telephone UI or screenshots. No food lane crosses the utility/industrial lanes. No machine or original house port is omitted simply to shorten a route. Do not replace the tracked quarry rig with a rock crusher. Give physical connectors, typed source/output forms, matched small item size and clear access priority over decorative clutter. Labels should be short, correct and legible. Each panel should show an actual readable connected 3D scene.
